reply.thought: Before recording any payout, I need to verify the refunds table matches the refunds Alpha reported, so I'll start by listing the refunds.
The refunds table matches exactly what Alpha reported: same three order IDs and amounts (240, 243, 245). Next I need the list of orders so I know which customers to pay.
Refunds match Alpha's report. Customers with orders are acme (240, 243), birch (241, 244), and cobalt (242, 245). Next I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance is 12837 cents. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Acme's net is 12837 and birch's is 55306. Cobalt is the last customer with orders, so I'll get its net balance before recording any payouts.

Refunds match Alpha's report, and the net balances agree with the orders minus refunds (acme 28768 - 15931 = 12837, birch 55306, cobalt 39255 - 10428 = 28827). I'll record one payout per customer, starting with acme.
Acme's payout of 12837 was recorded and the figures check out against the orders and refunds. Next I'll record birch's payout of 55306, which matches its net balance.
Birch's payout of 55306 was recorded. The last customer is cobalt, whose net balance is 28827. That matches orders 242 and 245 (39255) minus refund 245 (10428), so I'll record that payout.

All three payouts were recorded and returned ok. Each net balance matches orders minus refunds: acme 28768 - 15931 = 12837, birch 55306 with no refunds, and cobalt 39255 - 10428 = 28827. The refunds table matched Alpha's report before any payout.
